properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The `evp_bytestokey` npm package is the browser shim of OpenSSL's single-round MD5 EVP_BytesToKey KDF. It sits under browserify-aes in the crypto-browserify stack that webpack substitutes for node:crypto when react-scripts bundles web3.js for the browser (client/package-lock.json:3799-3819). Shipped with the client bundle; no application call site in the repo code. The KDF itself (single-round MD5) is weak, but it is used for AES key derivation inside library code paths this app does not invoke

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@0.10.0 (declared at client/package-lock.json:10194, required by selfsigned@1.10.11 at :13560) is the pure-JS crypto provider behind react-scripts/webpack-dev-server's self-signed HTTPS development certificate. node-forge ships RSA keygen/encrypt/sign, X.509, TLS 1.0-1.2 and AES. Dev toolchain surface; changeable here by upgrading react-scripts/selfsigned (node-forge 0.10.0 is an old release with known advisories). No application call site in the repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: `create-ecdh` ^4.0.0 is the crypto-browserify ECDH shim (implemented over the elliptic library, default curve secp256k1) that webpack bundles into web3.js's browser build. Classical elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman, Shor-vulnerable; shipped library surface with no application call site in this repo (the dApp signs transactions, it does not perform standalone key agreement).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl is genuinely declared in the client lockfile (0.14.5 at client/package-lock.json:14957, required by bcrypt-pbkdf@1.0.2 at :3666-3667 within react-scripts' sshpk/http-signature chain) and in the root lockfile (0.14.5 at package-lock.json:14848, truffle's tree). Note the dep_scan version claim of 1.0.3 is off — both lockfiles resolve 0.14.5 — but the package and its Ed25519/XSalsa20-Poly1305 surface are real. Shipped library surface; no application call site in the repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES (CBC/GCM/CTR) is provided by node-forge@0.10.0, declared at client/package-lock.json:10194 and consumed by selfsigned@1.10.11 (:13558-13560) for the webpack-dev-server HTTPS dev-cert path (also reachable via libp2p-crypto in the root lockfile:11414/:10152). Shipped library surface; no application call site in the repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge is declared in both lockfiles: client/package-lock.json:10194 (version 0.10.0, required by selfsigned@1.10.11 at :13560 — react-scripts/webpack-dev-server dev-cert stack) and root package-lock.json:11414 (required by libp2p-crypto@0.19.6 at :10152, optional, in truffle's tree). Pure-JS crypto provider shipping RSA, TLS 1.0-1.2, X.509, AES, HMAC, MD5/SHA. Old version with known advisories; changeable here by upgrading the consumers.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X.509 certificate generation/consumption is provided by node-forge@0.10.0 (client/package-lock.json:10194), consumed by selfsigned@1.10.11 to mint the webpack-dev-server's self-signed TLS certificate during local development. No committed .crt/.pem or CA bundles exist in the repo; this is toolchain-provided X.509, not application-managed PKI.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@3.0.1 is declared in the client lockfile as part of web3.js's ethereum-cryptography stack (client copy mirrors root package-lock.json:6947/:13836), where scrypt derives keystore-encryption keys for Ethereum wallet files. Password-based KDF, memory-hard, classical (not Shor-relevant but its output wraps secp256k1 private keys); shipped with the browser bundle, no application call site in the repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js@2.4.11 is the pure-JS SHA-1/SHA-224/256/384/512 implementation required by create-hash/create-hmac in the crypto-browserify stack that webpack bundles for web3.js's browser build (client/package-lock.json:4705, 4718 show the requires). Shipped dependency; SHA-1 is present in the library surface though the Ethereum stack uses SHA-256/keccak paths. No application call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 (client/package-lock.json:5569, requires bn.js, brorand, hash.js, hmac-drbg) is the pure-JS elliptic-curve library at the heart of web3.js's browser-side account handling: secp256k1 ECDSA for transaction/message signing and the curve behind create-ecdh. This is the primary classical crypto dependency of the client. properties.value: selfsigned@1.10.11 (client/package-lock.json:13558) requires node-forge ^0.10.0 and generates the self-signed X.509/RSA certificate that webpack-dev-server presents for local HTTPS in the react-scripts toolchain. Dev-only tooling surface; changeable here via react-scripts upgrade. No committed certificates in the repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 is required by elliptic@6.5.4 (client/package-lock.json:5576) — pure-JS SHA-2/RIPEMD-160 family used inside the web3.js signing stack (HMAC-DRBG seeding for ECDSA key generation and RIPEMD160 for Ethereum address derivation). Shipped with the browser bundle; no direct application call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2@3.1.2 is the browser pbkdf2 shim required by crypto-browserify (client/package-lock.json:4752 area) in web3.js's webpack bundle, and by ethereum-cryptography in the truffle lockfile (root package-lock.json:6949 — used with scrypt for Ethereum keystore files). Password-based KDF; shipped with both builds; no application call site in the repo.
